newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian commerce minister unhappy with rupee rate.
newsitem.headline: Indian commerce minister unhappy with rupee rate.

text.p: Indian Commerce Minister Bola Bulli Ramaiah said on Tuesday that he was not happy with the exchange rate of the rupee and the currency could be made fully convertible only after the country achieved a trade surplus.
Asked whether the rupee was at the right exchange rate level against the dollar, Ramaiah told reporters: "I am not happy but I have to see the overall situation."
At 12:26 p.m. (0656 GMT), the rupee was quoted at 35.812/820 against the U.S. dollar.
Exporters have been pressing the government to allow the rupee to depreciate to give them a trading advantage and boost overseas sales, which have been relatively sluggish this calendar year.
But the Finance Ministry and Reserve Bank of India are keen to keep inflation, which could be fuelled by a falling rupee, under control.
Asked when India would make the rupee fully convertible, the commerce minister said: "Full convertibility only when there is surplus on trade account."
India reported a merchandise trade deficit of $5.44 billion in 1996/97 (April-March), up from $4.54 billion in the previous fiscal year.
A Reserve Bank of India panel in June recommended steps that the government could take to make the rupee convertible on the capital account by the turn of the century.
The rupee was made convertible on the current account of the balance of payments in August 1994.

The panel listed preconditions for a fully convertible rupee, including an average inflation rate of three to five percent for the three-year period until 2000, and a reduction in the fiscal deficit as a share of gross domestic domestic (GDP) to 3.5 percent by 1999/2000.
India aims to cut the federal fiscal deficit to 4.5 percent of GDP in 1997/98 from 5.0 percent last year.
